title: PowerPoint (Desktop): reference SharePoint and OneDrive files when creating a presentation with Copilot Agent Mode
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, file-reference workflow and documented data protections are supported. The SharePoint control's navigation and PowerShell command are correct, and searches found no feature-specific availability switch, default, licence-tier statement or separate meter.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Copilot in PowerPoint can recognize a SharePoint or OneDrive file mentioned by file or document name in a prompt.
claims.quote: Copilot in PowerPoint can now recognize references to files stored in SharePoint and OneDrive when you mention them in your prompt, such as by file or document name.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The user can reference the file by document name and/or owner.
claims.quote: In your prompt, reference a file saved in SharePoint or OneDrive by the document name and/or owner of the document.

claims.claim: This workflow does not require manually attaching or uploading the file.
claims.quote: This update makes it easier to use relevant Microsoft 365 content without manually attaching or uploading the file.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Copilot can use the referenced file as context and create a presentation containing information from it.
claims.quote: You can naturally reference a relevant file in your prompt, and Copilot can use that file as context when creating your presentation.

claims.claim: The release notes say implicit file references were previously unsupported for these storage locations.
claims.quote: Previously, these implicit file references were not supported for files stored in these locations.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Scope: Files; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Copilot respects existing SharePoint and OneDrive permissions and references content the user is authorized to access.
claims.quote:
Copilot respects existing SharePoint and OneDrive permissions.
Permissions come first. Copilot only summarizes or references content that the user is already authorized to access.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Copilot can surface overshared content to anyone who has access.
claims.quote: If content is already overshared, Copilot can surface it to anyone who has access.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery governs organization-wide search and Microsoft Copilot discovery scenarios, including tenant-wide content discovery.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery affects organization-wide search experiences (SharePoint home, Office.com, Bing) and Microsoft Copilot discovery scenarios, including experiences that rely on tenant-wide content discovery.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery does not change existing permissions.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery doesn't change existing permissions.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery does not prevent users with permission from directly accessing content.
claims.quote: Users who already have access to content can continue to access that content directly.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: A DLP policy for Copilot can prevent summarization of labelled files and emails.
claims.quote: A DLP policy for Copilot can keep Copilot from summarizing labeled files and emails. Copilot can still return a link so the user can open the item outside Copilot.

claims.claim: Sensitivity-label-based DLP blocking of file processing is documented for Copilot in PowerPoint.
claims.quote:
Block files and emails with sensitivity labels from being processed
This feature is available in Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Chat, Cowork, and Copilot in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.

claims.claim: Items excluded by sensitivity-label DLP may appear in citations, but their content is not used in the response.
claims.quote: Identified items still appear in the citations of the response, but Copilot and Cowork don't access or use the content of the item in the response.

claims.claim: Copilot and agents cannot access unopened SharePoint and OneDrive documents labelled and encrypted with user-defined permissions, subject to the two stated exceptions.
claims.quote: Copilot and agents can't access unopened documents in SharePoint and OneDrive that are labeled and encrypted with user-defined permissions. There are two exceptions:

claims.claim: One exception is a default sensitivity label extending SharePoint permissions to downloaded documents.
claims.quote: the label is a default sensitivity label that extends SharePoint permissions to downloaded documents

claims.claim: The other exception is directly referencing the document by typing '/'.
claims.quote: or the user references the document directly by typing "/".

claims.claim: In both user-defined-permission exceptions, the user must also have the EXTRACT usage right.
claims.quote: In both cases, the user must also have the EXTRACT usage right.

claims.claim: The release-notes entry describes no action that modifies the source file.
claims.quote: Searched: read the complete 555895 release-notes entry for actions on the source file; it describes using the file as context and creating a presentation, not modifying the source.

claims.claim: The release-notes entry describes no write access to SharePoint or OneDrive for this workflow.
claims.quote: Searched: read the complete 555895 release-notes entry for write access to SharePoint or OneDrive; the entry describes references to stored files and presentation creation, not write access to these services.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The SharePoint admin center path is Sites > Active sites > site > Settings > Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote:
In the SharePoint admin center, expand Sites and select Active sites.
Select the site you want to configure.
Open the Settings tab, and then turn Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot on.

claims.claim: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true enables Restricted Content Discovery for a site.
claims.quote:
Enable Restricted Content Discovery for a site
Use PowerShell
Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is a general site-level SharePoint control rather than a control specific to this PowerPoint file-reference feature.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery is a site-level setting. When you turn on the setting, Microsoft 365 search systems propagate it so that content from the site doesn't appear in organization-wide discovery experiences.

claims.claim: Microsoft describes Restricted Content Discovery as intended for Copilot deployment and governance scenarios.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery is intended for Microsoft Copilot deployment and governance scenarios.

claims.claim: Changes to Restricted Content Discovery can take time to propagate through search and Copilot experiences.
claims.quote: Updates can take time to propagate throughout search and Microsoft Copilot experiences.

claims.claim: By default, only SharePoint administrators can manage Restricted Content Discovery.
claims.quote: By default, only SharePoint administrators can manage Restricted Content Discovery.

claims.claim: The described change concerns users creating presentations with Copilot in PowerPoint, not a change to workflows outside Copilot in PowerPoint.
claims.quote: You can now reference files saved in SharePoint libraries and OneDrive folders when creating a presentation with Copilot using Agent Mode in PowerPoint.
